subject: Stop regenerative disk churn at the writer: retire notebook-era producers before more GC

body.trigger: The Generation-10 repository-shape epoch is green but explicitly reports scheduled notebook writers still targeting transitional/notebook-era surfaces. Reclaiming their outputs without cutting over the producers creates a delete-regenerate loop.
required_actions: Inventory only scheduled/background writers whose destination belongs to retired notebook-era, recovery, verification, or generated-output locations moved by the RepositoryShape migration.

For each writer, map its output to the new explicit owner under evidence/ or generated/projections/; change the destination or disable the obsolete writer only when the new owner already preserves the required semantics.
Record a RegressionFence that no scheduled process may recreate a forbidden top-level peer after repository-shape validation.
After writer cutover, perform one bounded reclaim of now-orphaned old outputs and measure regenerated_bytes_since_last_sweep. Do not repeatedly delete the same regenerated class.

Defer the large transitional 10-Code compatibility-root cutover while ResourceWeather is tight unless it can be implemented as a low-write alias/import/path compatibility change. Preserve active epoch paths.
body.cross_graph_effect: RepositoryShape ownership becomes an input to ResourceGraph: a path with a retired owner and an active producer is a producer-divergence obligation, not merely a deletion candidate.
